questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Canada because I wanted safe place, that was different enough to be interesting but similar enough to Denmark as to not be to overwhelming. And I chose Toronto because they had the best university for math in Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university and the city was great, but a combination of a way to difficult course and a suppar housing situation made it less fund then I had hoped.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, no problem at all.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university hosted a guided tour and an information meeting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not particularly easy. I found mine through Homadorma, which was nice, since I knew it wasn’t a scam, but some of the information on the Homadorma page was wrong, as it had not been updated in a while, and they clearly hadn’t checked the accomadation after the initial verification. But I think the variance on quality varies a lot on Homadorma, so it is just a bit of a gamble.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure you can get to campus easily enough. I could bike ( 8 km) which was fine, as Toronto had enough bikelanes for that to be possible, but we didn’t have any snow either, so that would probably change things. In general it is probably important to live walking distance away from campus or a metro to campus, if you are going to Canada in the spring semester, as the snow can get quite intense.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I tried on campus housing, but couldn’t get in.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send an email with a questionaire that you had to complete before a certain deadline. Actually there was multiple emails, as you could register in later rounds if you didn’t get what you wanted initially or if you changed your mind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nice email service.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you meet the course prerequisites, and alternatively compare the prereqs to similar courses at KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great, I loved my logic courses (which are not avaliable at KU)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3rd and 4th level courses, but both of my 4th level courses were joint grad and undergrad courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: VERY similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Combinatorics, Introduction to logic, set theory and Riemannian Geometry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to logic and Set Theory as these two courses goes very well hand in hand, and are very interesting, and you can’t really get the same at KU. The courses give a nice view into the field of logic in math, which is often overlooked at KU, as most people here do Algebra, Analysis, Topology or Geometry.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many clubs, but I didn’t join any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every club imaginable, and lot’s of sports teams and fitness rooms/opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the museums in Toronto. They are great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Algonquin national park if you are able, and a must see is of course Naigra Falls.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. It is a lot like the US.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Canadians are very nice, so if you tell them you are an exchange students, then they become really friendly and chatty.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Canadians speak a lot in public (i.e. To strangers)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are nice, thoughtful and interesting. Toronto is also very diverse, so you will meet people from all over the world.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find good accomadation. Get a video tour before deciding on a place. Also start searching in late april or start may if you want housing close to campus (like Tartu).
2. Make friends with the locals, and go explore Toronto.
3. Remember to see some of the Canadian wilderness. You can quite far by train.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: U of T is a bit elitist, so you will probably have a bigger study load then at KU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The housing, and Riemannian Geometry.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
